problem_type: renderer importing main-process asset transport implementation
symptom: The Vite-backed Electron window showed the main-interface error boundary because the renderer transitively loaded @xmldom/xmldom from the main-process upload implementation.
direct_cause: catalogTaskActions imported the small collectLocalAssetUrls traversal from assetLocalization, pulling that module's Node buffers, upload policy, and CommonJS XML parser into the renderer module graph.
class_root: A shared pure value-classification operation lived behind a process-specific transport owner, so a renderer consumer crossed the Electron process boundary to reuse it.
affected_population: Developers running Nomi through the Vite Electron development entry
Electron walkthroughs that validate the same development renderer
Renderer generation tasks that collect local asset references
entry_points: Vite renderer module graph for the studio route

external_sources.purpose: Confirm @xmldom/xmldom is a Node-oriented XML DOM implementation whose documented runtime usage is not needed by the renderer's pure asset-value traversal.

invariants: Renderer code imports asset-value classification from the dependency-free assetValueScheme module and never from the upload/XML transport implementation.
collectLocalAssetUrls keeps one implementation and remains re-exported for existing main-process callers.
Vite-backed Electron reaches the project library without a pageerror from @xmldom/xmldom.

recurrence.reason: Any renderer import of a main-process transport module can pull Node-only parsers into Vite.
same_class_scan: Searched renderer imports of assetLocalization and @xmldom/xmldom.
Moved collectLocalAssetUrls to the dependency-free assetValueScheme owner.

prevention.strategy: Keep pure asset-value classification in assetValueScheme; renderer catalog tasks import that module only.

migration: No persisted-data migration. Only module ownership changes; asset detection and request payloads are unchanged.
residual_risks: Other renderer imports of main-process modules remain governed by the existing architecture gates and should be split at their pure boundary when found.
